News.title: Where is my polling station? How to find your place to vote in 2026 local elections and what time polls open
News.content:
MILLIONS of voters will head to the polls for local elections in early May, with more than 5,000 council seats being contested.

Here’s everything you need to know about finding your local polling station and what time the doors open and close, so you can have your say.





How do I find my polling station?

Polling stations are assigned based on where you live, with the address printed on the poll card that drops through your letterbox a few weeks before election day.

So the quickest way to track yours down is to check your poll card, which is sent out by your local council.

The card lists the address of the polling station you have been allocated, along with the date of the election and your ward name.

It’s important to remember that you can only vote at the polling station shown on your card – even if there is one closer to home, you will not be allowed to use it.



If you don’t have your card to hand, you can find out where to vote by entering your postcode on the Electoral Commission’s online tool.

It tells you where your polling station is, who is standing, and who to contact if you need help.

What time do polling stations open?

Polling stations across England will be open from 7am to 10pm on Thursday, May 7, 2026.

You can pop in to vote at any time during that 15-hour window.



If you are already inside the polling station, or even waiting in the queue outside when the doors close at 10pm, staff are required to let you cast your vote.

Most polling stations are set up in public buildings like schools, community centres, libraries or church halls.

To vote in person you will need to bring an accepted form of photo ID to vote, following changes to the law in 2023.

That includes a a UK passport, photocard driving licence, blue badge, and an older person’s bus pass, among others.

You also need to be registered to vote at your current address.



If you don’t have one of the accepted IDs, it is possible to apply for a free Voter Authority Certificate, but the deadline – 5pm on Tuesday, April 28 – has now passed.

The registration deadline to vote in the local elections – 11.59pm on Monday, April 20 – has also now passed.

What if I’ve lost my poll card?

You don’t actually need your poll card to vote.

As long as you are on the electoral register and bring an accepted form of photo ID, you will still be allowed to cast your ballot.

If you would like a replacement card or want to check your polling station details, you can contact your local council’s electoral services team.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Their contact details are listed on the Electoral Commission website by postcode, which is the same link as above.

If you can’t get to the polling station on the day, it is possible apply for a postal or proxy vote, but the April 21 deadline has now passed.

News.title: Shocking moment bloke calmly walks into hospital with a giant machete lodged in his head
News.content:
This is the shocking moment a man was caught on camera with a massive machete buried in his head.

Jaw-dropped bystanders watched in total disbelief as the young man casually scrolled on his phone despite a blade sticking out the side of his skull.





The victim, named only as Isma, was rushed to a Mumbai hospital in the early hours of Saturday morning after a horror attack.

He had been struck with a “koita” – a terrifying hooked blade usually used for hacking open coconuts or clearing thick scrub.

Medics were stunned to find the patient conscious and alert, showing no signs of brain fade despite the gruesome head wound.

Chilling scans later revealed the heavy metal blade had plunged nearly 1.5 inches deep into his brain.



A team of neurosurgeons led by Dr Batuk Diora raced against the clock to perform an emergency operation.

The surgeons pulled off a miracle to successfully remove the weapon while the patient was safely knocked out.



In a statement, local bosses confirmed the “operation was a success” and the brave patient is now on the road to recovery.

He is currently being monitored in a trauma ICU where his condition is said to be stable and improving by the day.

The “koita” is a notorious weapon in India, often measuring a whopping three to six feet in length.

The blades are often used in South Indian action films during dramatic fight scenes.

But in the real world, “koita gangs” have a much darker reputation for terrorising the streets of Maharashtra state.



Police are still hunting those responsible for the stomach-churning assault that left the victim inches from death.

News.title: Four in 10 Brits have turned to AI to write messages for sensitive occasions
News.content:
AI HELP Four in 10 Brits have turned to AI to write messages for sensitive occasions

FOUR in 10 Brits have turned to AI to write messages for life’s most sensitive occasions – including love letters, apologies, and condolences for a family loss.

A survey of 1,500 adults revealed the extent of the nation’s writer’s block when it comes to showing they care, with 50 per cent having delayed saying anything to a struggling friend or relative because they were so stuck for words.





This fear of saying the wrong thing has also resulted in 22 per cent never receiving a card during a difficult time in their life.

Which is a shame, as 64 per cent confirmed even a short message can be “deeply meaningful”, especially when having a bad day.

To stop the trend of saying ‘nothing at all’, 43 per cent are now looking to artificial intelligence to help generate messages of support or sympathy.

Georgie Smallwood, chief product and technology officer at Moonpig , which commissioned the research, said: “It’s clear even the briefest message or token can mean so much, so we are encouraging people to be braver in those situations when it’s difficult to know exactly what to say.

“While AI tools obviously can’t replace the human touch in these moments, they can be very helpful in scenarios when you really can’t seem to express yourself – there to push you in the right direction and get the words flowing, rather than write them all for you.

“It’s always better to say something than nothing, so take the help where you can get it for life’s difficult moments.”

The study reported 45 per cent find themselves completely lost for words during tough times, admitting they know they have emotions to express but struggle to put them on paper.

The worry of offending or upsetting someone is the primary cause of this hesitation, with 46 per cent saying they are held back by the fear of saying the wrong thing.



Further to this, 44 per cent admitted that writing a message to commemorate any key life moments, let alone sensitive ones, feels stressful.

A stark contrast has also been highlighted between different generations, as 25–34-year-olds are struggling the most – 61 per cent of this group admitted to delaying messages and 55 per cent to obsessively deleting and rewriting them before sending.

In comparison, only 37 per cent of over 55s reported the same hesitations.

It’s also the girls who find expressing themselves the hardest, with 49 per cent of women admitting that translating their thoughts into words is a challenge, compared to 41 per cent of men.

However, despite finding the writing process a challenge, women still find the written word easier than expressing their feelings in person.



They are significantly more likely than men to express deep emotions in a card or note rather than face-to-face (47 per cent versus 40 per cent).

Men, meanwhile, have embraced AI more readily to draft messages, being more likely than women to use tools for romantic notes (28 per cent vs 22 per cent) or to find the right words for an apology (26 per cent vs 22 per cent).

Georgie Smallwood, for Moonpig, added: “Every day, customers use our creative tools to help them write messages that really matter, expressing their care, support, sadness, or just to check in and let someone know they’re loved.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“One in two cards sent we send are created using our personalisation tools, making them completely unique.

“It really feels special that we are helping people to stay in touch and say the right thing at the right time.”

News.title: Horror moment Brit ‘stabs hotel worker’ in Bali before security guard leaps on car bonnet to stop him fleeing
News.content:
DRAMATIC video footage shows the moment a British man allegedly stabs a hotel worker in Bali.

Indonesian police have arrested Aaron Michel, 35, from London, accused of attacking the worker at the luxury Dynasty Resort on the remote Menjangan Island, off the north-west tip of the holiday destination.





Michel was arrested in Bali’s port town of Gilimanuk, where police believe he was attempting to flee by boat to the nearby island of Java.

According to Bali police, Michel arrived on Menjangan Island, which is popular with tourists and famous for its barking deer that lounge in the sea, at about 8pm Tuesday night.

Buleleng Police Chief, Ruzi Gusman, said: “He arrived at the Dynasty Resort parking are at 8pm, got out of the car and walked towards the front office. A few minutes later, he returned to the parking lot.

“He was approached by the front office employee and the suspect pulled a knife from his pants and stabbed the worker.”

Hotel car park CCTV shows Michel and the hotel worker talking by his car before Michel appears to pull out what looks like a long blade.

The footage captures the moment the two men scuffle before Michel allegedly stabs the worker with the knife.

The pair then disappear off camera.

Seconds later Michel is seen running back to his white Suzuki chased by the worker.



He drives off and the worker jumps on the car bonnet in an attempt to stop him, before being thrown off.

“Michel was arrested on Tuesday night at 11.37 pm in the Gilimanuk port as he was attempting to flee Bali,” Chief Gusman said.

“We also confiscated two knives and the white Suzuki that he was driving.”



Michel is now held in police custody and being questioned by officers.

The stabbing victim, a local male who has not been named, was evacuated from the tiny island and rushed to Bali’s main hospital in Denpasar where he is undergoing treatment in ICU.

With more than six million international visitors annually, Bali has become a popular destination for Brits.



But the influx of millions of “cashed up” holidaymakers has transformed the once tranquil holiday destination into a crime hotspot.

The island has rapidly emerged as a honey pot for international drug traffickers and street violence and robbery is on the rise.

News.title: Mum who left young brother and sister to die on ground after fleeing fatal e-scooter crash AVOIDS jail
News.content:
TRAGIC SMASH Mum who left young brother and sister to die on ground after fleeing fatal e-scooter crash AVOIDS jail

A MUM who fled a horror crash that killed a young brother and sister while they were on an e-scooter has avoided jail.

Roman Casselden, 16, and nine-year-old Darcie were struck by Deimante Ziobryte’s Audi.





But instead of stopping to check on the youngsters, the 21-year-old “continued to drive and didn’t stop”.

Ziobryte eventually pulled over but rang family members instead of phoning the police.

Roman and Darcie tragically could not be saved and died from catastrophic injuries at the scene in Pitsea, Essex.

Ziobryte, who has recently given birth, wept today as she was sentenced for failing to stop at the scene of a collision.



Essex Police said previously she would face no further action in relation to a possible offence of causing death by dangerous driving.

She avoided jail and was instead handed a three month sentence suspended for 12 months.



In an emotional victim impact statement, Roman and Darcie’s mum Emma Keeling said she has had “sleepless nights every night”.

“I will never be the same person again because of it,” the heartbroken mum added.

The children’s dad, Alec Casselden, said he had “nightmares of them lying in the road alone”.

He said: “Why would she leave two children to die and drive off?”

Prosecutor Rohini Majumdar said she was driving an Audi when Darcie and Roman came to a junction on the e-scooter.



She added: “The defendant swerved to avoid a collision but unfortunately they made contact and the two youths on the e-scooter have suffered fatal injuries as a result.

“Following this collision the defendant has continued to drive and failed to stop until they got to a lane nearby where they stopped the car and made multiple phone calls to family members, not to police or the emergency services.

“At no point did the defendant return to the scene of the collision to speak to police.”

Hulusi Ali, mitigating, said the horror was a “panic-driven failure in the aftermath of a catastrophic event.”

He read from a letter from Ziobryte in which said she wanted to express “my sincere remorse”.



“I’ve relived the events every day and I know I will carry the weight of these events with me for the rest of my life,” she added.

Inquests into the deaths of Roman and Darcie heard that both siblings died of traumatic head injury.

Essex area coroner Michelle Brown said emergency services attended and Darcie was pronounced dead at 7.10pm and Roman at 7.50pm.

As well as a suspended sentence, Ziobryte was ordered to complete 80 hours of unpaid work, 20 rehabilitation activity requirement days and pay a total of £239 in costs and victim surcharge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She banned her from driving for three years, but the court heard she “doesn’t want to drive a motor vehicle ever again”.



Sentencing, deputy district judge Jennifer Twite said: “This is clearly an incredibly sad case.”

News.title: Mysterious network of secret tunnels found beneath quaint UK village after locals spent decades thinking them a myth
News.content:
TUNNEL VISION Mysterious network of secret tunnels found beneath quaint UK village after locals spent decades thinking them a myth

A MYSTERIOUS network of secret tunnels beneath a quaint UK village – thought to be just local folklore – has been found.

Shocked local enthusiasts in the Oxfordshire village of Bloxham have confirmed the long-rumoured passages do exist.





The group, known as the Bloxham Underground Tunnel Society, was set up in 2024 following discussion online about the so-called myth.

Since then the team has been on a mission to uncover the truth.

Now they have made a series of breakthroughs which reveal the winding tunnels beneath the village on the edge of the Cotswolds.

Images show narrow walkways snaking underground, with clear signs the passages have been there for centuries.





Experts are still unsure why the tunnels were built.

One theory suggests they may have been used as escape routes during the persecution of Catholics in the Reformation hundreds of years ago.

Local resident Dave Green, chairman of the society, said his team were “very excitable” when they found the first “spooky” tunnel.

“Like most villages in the country, there’s always myths,” he told the Daily Mail.

“But a lot of people never record anything – it’s just talked about through their parents and grandparents.



“We decided to follow the myths. People tend to rubbish them – they say they’re ridiculous and not true.”

Dave believes many more tunnels in Bloxham are waiting to be found.

He revealed the first discovery came after speaking to elderly residents, while the second was a complete accident.

A small hidden door in a garden wall led to the first tunnel, which the homeowner knew about but had never explored.

Cavers from Birmingham University were called in to carry out safety checks before the team ventured inside with headtorches.



Their first expedition in August last year uncovered a 40ft tunnel with blocked-off channels branching from it.

Mr Green said: “When we went in we noticed a difference in the air. There was a few of us in there so the breathing took some adjusting. But it was a fantastic feeling.”

A second, much larger tunnel was discovered in March this year when the ground suddenly gave way beneath a builder laying foundations for a garage.

That passage stretched an incredible 130ft and appeared to lead to hidden chambers and caverns buried under rubble.

Dave believes the passages could date back as far as medieval times, meaning they may be over 500 years old.



Finds inside the tunnels back up the theory, with the team uncovering fossils, pottery, Victorian glass bottles and even animal bones, including what is believed to be a red deer skull.

Red deer have not been common in the area for centuries, suggesting the tunnels have existed for a “considerable” length of time.

The group now hopes to carbon date the bones to pin down the tunnels’ true age.

Strange carvings have also been spotted etched into the stone, including a double V symbol known as “virgo virginum”, believed in the Middle Ages to ward off evil spirits.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The society, made up of Dave Green, Martin Wyatt, Tom Smith, Martin Whytto, Simon Finch and Jim Smithson, say they have already identified more sites to explore.



And with further digs planned, they believe even more of Bloxham’s hidden underground network could soon be revealed.

News.title: Kim Jong-un officially SCRAPS goal of reunifying North and South Korea after 70 years
News.content:
TYRANT Kim Jong Un has officially ripped up the rulebook on peace by scrubbing all talk of uniting with the South from his nation’s constitution.

The dictator has binned the 70-year-old goal of peaceful reunification, rebranding the North as a completely separate country for the first time since the 1940s.





This move was exposed by experts at a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday after secret documents were leaked by an academic, according to the Financial Times.

The new law explicitly defines Kim’s territory as bordering China and Russia to the north and the Republic of Korea to the south.

Experts say this is a massive shift, as Pyongyang has finally accepted that the peninsula is now two separate states at war.

For decades, the North maintained a constitutional mandate to achieve peaceful reunification with the South.



This national goal was established in the bitter aftermath of the 1945 division and the subsequent Korean War.

But the hermit nation has now gone silent on the changes, refusing to comment on the text revealed by South Korea‘s Unification Ministry.



While the new wording is not openly aggressive, analysts warn it’s a tactical move to treat the South like any other foreign enemy.

Top analyst Christopher Green told the Financial Times that Kim is trying to make North Korea look like a normal state.

He said: “Normal states define their adversaries in defence white papers and defence reviews and the like; they do not define their adversaries in the constitution.”



Kim’s rhetoric has shifted in recent years, repeatedly framing North and South Korea as separate countries, even going so far as to rename Tongil (“reunification”) metro station in Pyongyang and dismantling an Arch of Reunification monument.

The updated constitution also signals a looming battle over the “Northern Limit Line” in the Yellow Sea.

Pyongyang has never liked this sea border, claiming it was forced on them by the UN and the US after the 1953 Korean War ceasefire.

By changing the law, Kim is setting the stage for potential “future clashes” over these disputed waters.



In a shocking break with the past, Kim has even scrubbed the names of his own father and grandfather from the document’s title.

He has also deleted old slogans about the “revolutionary struggle” against “imperialist invaders” from the West.

Most terrifyingly, the new rules give Kim absolute, personal authority over the country’s nuclear red button and can now delegate nuke decisions to a shadowy state command.



This follows Kim’s new nuclear doctrine which allows the launch of a pre-emptive nuclear strike even if he’s only attacked with basic, conventional weapons.

He’s also pledged to beef up his nuclear stockpile after a record-breaking April saw the most missile tests in over two years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

While Kim rattles his sabres, South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung is still begging for the “flowers of peace” to bloom.

But Kim has ghosted every olive branch, and has repeatedly called the South its greatest enemy.

News.title: Ban on popular weedkiller feared to be linked to cancer is considered across UK – and it could risk you £5000
News.content:
A POPULAR weedkiller could be banned in the UK – following a new trade deal with the EU.

The chemical has been illegal in Europe since 2023.





A new European Union trade deal could lead to restrictions on the use of the weedkiller glyphosate in the UK.

Glyphosate is a popular herbicide which is typically used in industrial farming, including in wheat, oats and other cereals, and can be found in household weedkiller brands such as Roundup.

It has been linked to cancer and other health concerns by the World Health Organization, leading the EU to ban the chemical in 2023.

Now, the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) are in talks with the EU over a new sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) agreement.



This agreement covers a range of industries, including the production and movement of plants, animals and their products, food and feed safety as well as regulation of pesticides and biocides.

In the UK, around 50 councils are entirely pesticide-free in these areas, and using the banned chemical could lead to fines of up to £5000.

Environmental advocates said the government should use the deal to end the use of glyphosate completely.

The campaign coordinator for The Soil Association, Cathy Cliff, said: “Experts are increasingly warning that there is no ‘safe dose’ of glyphosate, meaning the chemical should be removed from our food.



“It’s time to cut the chemicals from our food and fields.”

According to The Guardian, glyphosate was found in more than 28% of UK bread samples tested in 2024.

However, Defra spokesperson commented: “Like all pesticides, glyphosate is subject to strict regulation.”

The talks with the EU, and subsequent push for a ban, comes ahead of the weedkiller’s licence renewal in December.

News.title: Jet2, easyJet, TUI, Ryanair and Wizz Air, Wednesday afternoon update for people with flights booked
News.content:
Jet2, easyJet, TUI, Ryanair and Wizz Air, Wednesday afternoon update for people with flights booked

The Department for Transport has issued an update for anyone planning on travelling over the next few months

View 3 Images People preparing to fly this summer have been issued an update

People who are preparing to fly have been issued an update by the government. The Department for Transport has responded to concerns of many people with flights booked ready for the summer holidays.

‌



Many are concerned of potential cancellations as a result of fuel shortages caused by the conflict in the Middle East. However the government has stepped in to give an update on what action people need to take.

‌



In an updated statement issued on Wednesday afternoon it insisted people shoud not currently look to make changes. It said: "UK airlines say that they are not currently seeing a shortage of jet fuel. The government is working with industry and international partners to keep passengers moving.

‌



View 3 Images People are preparing for their summer breaks (Image: Jonathan Raa/Getty Images)

"There is no current need for passengers to change their travel plans. UK airlines buy jet fuel in advance, and airports maintain stocks to support their resilience. The government is working closely with the aviation industry to monitor risks and minimise disruption to passengers.

"If your flight is cancelled, you have clear legal rights, including the right to a full refund or re-routing. Read this factsheet for the full picture on the current situation and what it means for you."

‌



It went on to answer some key question people have been asking. This is what it said:

Is there a shortage of jet fuel in the UK?

"UK airlines are clear that they are not currently seeing a shortage of jet fuel. It is typically bought in advance, with airports and their suppliers keeping stocks of bunkered fuel to support their resilience."

Do you need to change your travel plans?

"There is no current need to change upcoming travel plans. Government regularly meets with industry to monitor risks, understand pressures and ensure clear communication with passengers, should circumstances change.

‌



"We recognise that families may be concerned, and that aviation and tourism businesses are operating in challenging global conditions. We are working hand‑in‑hand with industry to help flights keep operating.

"We advise passengers to continue checking with their airlines before they travel, and to check the FCDO travel advice for the latest updates. You should also ensure you have appropriate travel insurance."

Are airlines cancelling lots of flights?

"While there has been media reporting on flights cancelled internationally in May, data from Cirium shows 120 UK flights have been cancelled, which is only 0.53% of the planned flights for the month. The majority of these UK cancellations are to and from the Middle East due to the conflict.

‌



"This is within the range of the number of cancellations we would expect in a normal year, and we continue to monitor the situation. In previous years, we typically saw around 1% of all flights arriving or departing from the UK cancelled, based on the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) punctuality statistics. Data from Cirium shows that only up to 0.2% of flights have been cancelled from June to August."

How is the government protecting passengers?

Under UK law, if your flight is cancelled, you are entitled to either a full refund or to be booked onto an alternative flight if you:

View 3 Images Summer is one of the busiest times for travel (Image: Josep Lago/Getty Images)

‌



depart from an airport in the UK on any airline

arrive at an airport in the UK on an EU or UK airline

arrive at an airport in the EU on a UK airline

For more information about your rights, you can:

‌



What is government doing?

"Since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, we have been closely monitoring UK jet fuel stocks and working with airlines, airports and fuel suppliers to ensure passengers keep moving and businesses are supported. We continue to plan for a range of contingencies, while focusing on securing a long lasting and workable solution to get shipping flowing freely again through the Strait of Hormuz."

How are airlines being supported?

"At some UK airports, airlines are given scheduled times known as ‘slots’ in which to take off or land. Under normal rules, airlines must use at least 80% of their allocated slots during a season to keep them for the following year. If they fall below this threshold, those slots can be reassigned to another airline. This is known as the ‘use it or lose it’ rule.

"Airport Coordination Limited, the independent body that manages slot allocation at UK airports, has updated its guidance so that airlines will not lose their slots if fuel shortages prevent them from flying. Airlines can now apply for an exemption from the ‘use it or lose it’ rule in these circumstances.

Article continues below

"The government is also seeking industry views on slot rules for the summer 2026 and winter 2026 seasons. The temporary measures would allow airlines to consolidate schedules on routes with multiple flights to the same destination on the same day.

"This means airlines can better plan ahead and focus on minimising disruption for passengers. It can also reduce fuel consumption by consolidating passengers onto fewer flights, rather than feeling pressure to operate flights purely to protect their slots."

News.title: 'Donald Trump told me my son "deserved to die" over support for Epstein file release'
News.content:
'Donald Trump told me my son "deserved to die" over support for Epstein file release'

Donald Trump's once-fiercest supporter, Marjorie Taylor Greene, has accused the president of saying her son deserved to be killed after she pushed for the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files

View 4 Images Marjorie Taylor Greene speaks out in support of Epstein victims, demanding the release of files she claims the White House moved to suppress. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump has been accused of telling his once-fieriest supporter she would "deserve" it if her son were murdered after she received death threats over her push to release the Epstein files.

‌



The explosive allegation was made by the former congresswoman, Marjorie Taylor Greene, during a speech in which she detailed the collapse of her once-close relationship with the US President. The former lawmaker, long regarded as Trump’s fiercest supporter and among the loudest voices in the MAGA movement, said the threats began after he publicly branded her a “traitor” during a dispute over the release of the US government files on Jeffrey Epstein.

‌



Greene alleged the president, who was once a close friend of the paedophile, pressured lawmakers and the Justice Department not to release the files. It came despite his pledge to do so while campaigning to retake the White House.

‌



View 4 Images Donald Trump and Marjorie Taylor Greene together when she was regarded as one of his most loyal and vocal supporters. (Image: AP)

‌



Recounting an alleged phone call she received from Trump in her congressional office ahead of a meeting to force the files' release, Greene said: "I’ll never forget it. He said, ‘Marjorie, you’re going to have to take your name off that discharge petition… This is a hoax. It’s a Democrat hoax, and we’ve got to just put this away and stop doing this.

"And he said, ‘My friends are going to get hurt. He said his friends would get hurt if we released the Epstein files. He said, ‘Marjorie, these are good people. These are people you know at Mar-a-Lago. People in Palm Beach. They’re going to get hurt by this.’"

Speaking to supporters, Greene then detailed how the abuse escalated into threats against her youngest son after Trump called her a “traitor”. She claimed she forwarded the messages directly to senior figures in the Trump administration, including Vice President JD Vance, FBI Director Kash Patel, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and deputy chief of staff James Blair.

‌



She told the audience: “I started getting death threats, and it was about me being called a traitor. It was, ‘You’re a traitor. You deserve to die. You’re a traitor. We’re going to kill you. You’re a traitor.’ “But it was the one that came in and they kept coming on, my son, my youngest, my baby boy: ‘We’re going to snuff out his life. We’re going to put a bullet in his head. Marjorie Traitor Greene.’”

The mum-of-three said she received little response from some of the administration’s most senior officials. Prompting laughter from the crowd, she added: "I got no response from Susie Wiles, none, and she’s a mother and a grandmother and a woman. I got no response from James Blair, because he only cares about making money on campaigns. I did hear from Kash Patel, he said, ‘On it,’ but I haven’t heard from him since. I don’t know what he’s on."

View 4 Images Jeffrey Epstein, the paedophile whose secret files have sparked a furious row between the President and one of his closest former allies (Image: US Department of Justice/AFP via)

‌



But Greene reserved her most serious allegation for Trump himself. “And then I heard back from Donald Trump. And I saved these text messages; I’d probably get put in jail if I released them publicly, but I saved them,” Greene said. "Donald Trump proceeded to tell me it was my fault and that I deserve it. If my son gets killed, I deserve it because I was a traitor to him. That is our President of the United States. That’s the man that says MAGA is whatever he wants it to be.”

Greene went on to question the movement she once helped champion so aggressively, saying many Americans had turned to Trump after losing faith in both major political parties. “That’s the man that, think about it, so many Americans turn to because they were failed by the Democrat Party and failed by the Republican Party. That’s the man that we elected to change everything,” she said.

The former congresswoman has not publicly released the alleged text messages. The extraordinary public break marks a dramatic reversal for Greene, who rose to prominence as one of Trump’s most loyal defenders after being elected to Congress in 2020.

‌



He endorsed her successful 2022 re-election campaign and Greene was a prominent figure on the campaign trail during the 2024 presidential race. But relations between the pair deteriorated sharply over the Epstein files issue, with Greene increasingly accusing Trump of blocking transparency to protect powerful associates.

Her resignation from Congress earlier this year came shortly after Trump publicly denounced her. Trump has denied any wrongdoing in relation to his friendship with Epstein and insisted the since-released documents “totally exonerated” him.

View 4 Images Side by side on the 2024 campaign trail, the pair appeared inseparable - few could have predicted the bitter and very public falling-out that would follow (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

In a statement responding to Greene's allegations, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle called her “a quitter who is pathetically trying to stay relevant” by bashing Trump, adding “unfortunately, Trump Derangement Syndrome has rotted former Congresswoman Greene’s peanut-sized brain.”

The White House did not directly address the specifics of Greene’s allegation.

News.title: ‘Horror fall ended up with amputation, so I threw a goodbye party for my leg’
News.content:
‘Horror fall ended up with amputation, so I threw a goodbye party for my leg’

When a freak accident saw Jim Britt need to have his leg amputated, it was an incredible shock. But advice came from the most unexpected place - his six year old granddaughter...

View 4 Images After he broke his leg while gardening, Jim was supported by his wife Anne

As the branch he was sawing gave way, Jim Britt’s ladder toppled and he plummeted to the ground. In a heap atop the soil, he remembers seeing two things. The first, his leg pointing the wrong way, with his shin bone protruding from the skin. The second, his wife Anne running towards him. “Strangely I felt no pain, I must have been in shock,” says Jim, 76, of the accident in October 2024. A retired NHS manager, he lives in Didsbury, Manchester, with Anne, 67, a garden designer, and their dog Betty and their two cats, Bobbi and Boo.

‌

Minutes later an air ambulance landed in the park beside the couple’s home and medics rushed to Jim’s side. He was transferred to Manchester Royal Infirmary where he underwent several operations to try to fix his leg.

‌



View 4 Images Jim and Anne outside Bridge End Cottage, where they threw a going away party for his leg

‌



But while the surgeons did everything they could, the next year proved hard for Jim, who was released from hospital just before Christmas 2024. “I was 74, and my circulation isn’t good. So I didn’t heal as well as perhaps I once would have. It was a long and painful process,” says Jim, who learned to walk again as best he could.

But in 2026 doctors broke the news he’d been dreading. His bones hadn’t knitted together, his leg wasn’t healing - and in fact it was getting worse - it would need to come off below the knee.

“Hearing that I was going to have to have my leg amputated was really shocking, even though I could see and feel it wasn’t right. I broke down, but my family surrounded me with hugs and kisses and promised me everything would be ok,” says Jim.

‌



The former NHS manager felt down for days, struggling to come to terms with the op, which was scheduled for the end of January. But then his granddaughter Molly said something that made him see things in a different way.

View 4 Images Jim and family celebrated all his leg had allowed him to do over the years

“She put her hand to my face and said, ‘But grandad, you can get a better leg now. And it’ll be shiny’ - and she was right. So Jim decided to reframe his amputation into something positive, and invited his family to a party - a send off for his leg.

‌



Choosing Bridge End Cottage in Cumbria, an accessible offering from elite holiday rental company Sykes Cottage, he sent out invitations and began planning. He bought balloons, banners and champagne. "I wanted to toast to everything that my leg had done for me,” says Jim. “It had worked so hard over the last 76 years, climbing mountains, running after my children and grandchildren and chasing my dogs down the beach. It deserved a good sendoff.”

The family arrived at Bridge End Cottage in mid-January, a week before Jim’s op. The house was immaculately cleaned, spacious, and with a downstairs easily accessed by Jim on his crutches. It was a great base to explore the southern lakes, with a river at the bottom of the garden and a pub at the end of the road serving delicious dinners and well-poured Guinness. Further down the road, was Fell Foot, a National Trust car park and picnic area at the southern end of Lake Windermere - the ideal place to start a walk, or simply sit on the beach.

View 4 Images Bridge End Cottage from Sykes Cottages

‌



And that’s exactly what they did. Jim and family sat on the stones, skimming them into the water, and said thank you to his leg.

“Molly was thankful it gave her a place to sit,” says Jim. “Anne was grateful it had propelled me on hike after hike over the years. And my daughter Hannah said she’d never forget how once when we went to Zanzibar and walked through an urchin-laden coral reef, it came out looking like something you’d find in a service station sandwich. She does have a way with words…”

*Prices start from £608 for seven nights at Bridge End Cottage. For more information, see sykescottages.co.uk

News.title: Virus outbreak on cruise 'linked to couple's birdwatching trip to landfill site'
News.content:
Hantavirus outbreak on cruise may be linked to couple's trip to landfill site

Two Argentine government officials investigating the origins of the hantavirus outbreak on board the MV Hondius cruise ship have said it may be linked to a couple's birdwatching tour at a landfill

View 2 Images The Dutch couple visited a landfill site in Ushuaia, on the Tierra del Fuego (Image: Getty Images)

The hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship may have begun with a couple's birdwatching trip to a landfill site before they both later died.

‌



Two officials investigating the deadly viral outbreak aboard the vessel have said that the virus may have gotten onto the ship after a Dutch couple went to a landfill site in Ushuaia, on the Tierra del Fuego, before boarding the boat.

‌



At St. Helena, the body of the Dutch man suspected to be the first hantavirus case on board was taken off the ship. His wife flew to South Africa, where she collapsed at the Johannesburg airport and died.

‌



The two Argentine officials spoke on condition of anonymity, telling the Associated Press that the couple may have been exposed to rodents at the landfill site. Authorities previously said Ushuaia and surrounding Tierra del Fuego province had never recorded a hantavirus case.

The news comes as a British doctor with suspected hantavirus was medically evacuated from the cruise ship today. The Brit, a Dutch crew member and another passenger, were taken from the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius for onward travel to the Netherlands, the World Health Organisation (WHO) has now confirmed.

‌



View 2 Images (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The three people evacuated were a 41-year-old Dutch national, a 56-year-old British national and a 65-year-old German national, The Dutch foreign ministry said, adding they would be "immediately transferred to specialized hospitals in Europe."

Two "remain in a serious condition," cruise ship operator Oceanwide Expeditions said, while the third had no symptoms but was "closely associated" with a German passenger who died on board the ship on May 2.

Article continues below

The evacuation means the ship can now continue on its three-day journey to the Canary Islands after Spanish authorities gave permission for the boat to dock. But a row has erupted with the president of the Canary Islands expressing concern over the ship docking in Tenerife.

Tour operator Oceanwide Expeditions said in a statement: “At this stage, the planned destination for m/v Hondius following the successful medical transfer is the Canary Islands.

“Oceanwide Expeditions remains in close and continual discussion with relevant authorities regarding our exact point of arrival, quarantine and screening procedures for all guests, and a precise timeline."

News.title: NHS '6 hour' rule for people who may wake up repeatedly tonight
News.content:
NHS '6 hour' rule for people who may wake up repeatedly tonight

The NHS has a '6-hour rule' that could help you get more rest if you are facing a poor night of sleep tonight, Wednesday, May 6

View 4 Images The NHS has a '6-hour' rule for people who struggle to sleep at night (Image: Milan_Jovic via Getty Images)

The NHS has guidance for those who might find themselves repeatedly waking up tonight. If people find themselves waking from sleep again and again, or rising up early and not being able to get back to sleep, it could be a warning sign.

‌



If you lie awake at night, or simply find it hard to get to sleep on Wednesday, May 6 or indeed any other night, this too could be a red flag. And not only will it leave you feeling tired and irritable, it can also have serious health consequences - increasing the risk of heart attack, stroke, type 2 diabetes and other conditions.

‌



Insomnia is a widespread issue across the UK. NHS Inform reports that roughly 1 in 3 people are affected by the condition.

‌



It is especially prevalent amongst older adults and can carry serious health implications. According to Harvard Medical School, poor sleep can have "profound consequences for our long-term health" - and people struggling tonight or indeed any night should follow simple steps below that could help - including an NHS '6-hour' rule.

The medical school's researchers warn that those who consistently fail to get adequate sleep face a heightened risk of chronic illness. Their Division of Sleep Medicine states: "What many people do not realize is that a lack of sleep-especially on a regular basis-is associated with long-term health consequences, including chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, and heart disease, and that these conditions may lead to a shortened life expectancy."

View 4 Images Insomnia affects many people in the UK (Image: mixetto via Getty Images)

‌



The NHS has put together guidance for those who struggle to drift off and who might face a restless night of broken sleep. The NHS website offers a handy '6 hour' rule for anyone finding themselves in this predicament.

The site advises: "Do not smoke or drink alcohol, tea or coffee at least 6 hours before going to bed." But there are several other steps they suggest people take to address poor sleep.

In fact, the health service has a list of do's and don'ts for people who struggle to sleep at night. When it comes to things you should do, the NHS says you should only go to bed when you're sleepy.

‌



View 4 Images You may need to see a doctor if you are suffering with the symptoms of insomnia (Image: MartinPrescott via Getty Images)

It also advises that you should wake up and get out of bed at the same time every day. You should also relax at least 1 hour before bed – for example, take a bath or read a book.

The NHS also advises making sure your bedroom is dark and quiet. It recommends using curtains, blinds, an eye mask or ear plugs if needed.

‌



People should also exercise regularly during the day. Finally, make sure your mattress, pillows and covers are comfortable.

What should I not do if I struggle to sleep at night?

The NHS advises you should not nap during the day. Its website also warns: "Do not watch television or use devices, like smartphones, right before going to bed, because the blue light makes you more awake."

You should also avoid eating a big meal late at night. You should in addition avoid exercise at least 4 hours before bed.

‌



The NHS also says that you should not sleep in after a bad night's sleep – stick to your regular sleeping hours instead. Finally, it notes that people should not drive when they feel sleepy.

How do you know if you have insomnia?

The NHS says that you have insomnia if you regularly:

wake up several times during the night

lie awake at night

find it hard to nap during the day even though you're tired

find it difficult to concentrate during the day because you're tired

feel tired and irritable during the day

still feel tired after waking up

find it hard to go to sleep

wake up early and cannot go back to sleep

‌



Insomnia lasting less than 3 months is referred to as short-term insomnia. Anything persisting for 3 months or more is classified as long-term insomnia. Sleep requirements vary from person to person, with the NHS recommending that adults get between 7 to 9 hours per night.

The most frequently reported triggers of insomnia include stress, anxiety or depression; noise, uncomfortable beds, or a room that's too hot or cold; illegal drugs such as cocaine or ecstasy; jet lag, alcohol, caffeine or nicotine; and shift work.

Insomnia can also contribute to obesity. Harvard Medical School state: "Several studies have linked insufficient sleep and weight gain. For example, studies have shown that people who habitually sleep less than six hours per night are much more likely to have a higher than average body mass index (BMI) and that people who sleep eight hours have the lowest BMI."

‌



The Cleveland Clinic says it can also lead to high blood pressure, depression, anxiety, obstructive sleep apnea and conditions that involve psychosis.

Can I cure my insomnia?

The Cleveland Clinic states that the primary treatment methods for insomnia consist of:

Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)

Medications (sleeping pills)

‌



It notes: "In general, your healthcare provider is the best person to tell you about your options and what they recommend. They can also explain possible side effects of medications."

View 4 Images There is guidance people can follow to try to tackle their insomnia (Image: Jacob Wackerhausen via Getty Images)

The Sleep Foundation also notes: "Treatment for insomnia depends on how long a person has been experiencing sleep issues and any specific factors that are contributing to their sleep loss. If insomnia is associated with another condition, such as sleep apnea or depression, treatment of the other condition often improves sleep.

Article continues below

"It is important to get help with insomnia sooner than later. For people with short-term insomnia, care may be focused on discussing practices to support sleep hygiene. Temporary use of a prescription sleep aid may be an option if the insomnia is causing high levels of concern or distress. People with insomnia may also benefit from cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).

"A few treatment approaches are available for people with insomnia that persists for weeks or months."

News.title: German tourist loses 6am race for sun lounger - but wins payout instead
News.content:
German tourist loses 6am race for sun lounger - but wins payout instead

A dad who spent over £6,000 on a Greek island holiday for his family sued a travel company after he couldn't find sun loungers for wife and kids despite waking up at 6am

View 2 Images A German tourist sued a travel company after he was unable to get sun loungers on holiday despite waking up at 6am (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A furious German tourist went to court and won a payout after he failed to get a sun lounger on holiday, despite waking up at 6am.

‌



The dad-of-two said he dropped around £6,200 (€7,186) on a package holiday to the Greek island of Kos with his two children and wife, back in August 2024. The man, who was not named, said he spent around 20 minutes each day trying to find sun loungers where all four family members could sit together. He said most sunbeds had already been taken by guests who put their towels down, despite the hotel having a rule explicitly against this.

‌



The dad, who sued a tour operator at a district court in Hanover, said even at 6am most of the sunbeds had been "taken" meaning his two kids were often forced to lie on the floor.

‌



Jet2 holiday update for all passengers with flights booked from end of May READ MORE :

View 2 Images The traveller said his kids were forced to sit on the floor on some days (stock image) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

He also claimed workers at the hotel failed to intervene and enforce their own policy against reserving spots with a towels in advance.

The furious man took the case to a German court and the judge sided with him, as the court found the package holiday was "defective" as the family did not get the "character" they would have expected as a contractual right.

‌



While the tour operator did not run the large Greek hotel the family had been staying at, the judge said it had an obligation to make sure each customer could have access to a sunbed during their stay.

The judge also said the travel company needed to make sure the hotel could ensure there was a "reasonable" ratio of sun loungers to tourists.

This tour operator, which was not named, was forced to give the dad a refund of £850 (€986.70) and it initially only paid £300 (€350). This major ruling comes weeks before Brits are set to kick off their Summer holidays, with similar pool and beach resorts popular with many UK tourists.

‌



The phenomena of the so-called "dawn dash", where people wake up early to secure sunbeds, is nothing new. Last Summer, holidaymaker Ben Smith said he was left gobsmacked when he discovered the prime loungers were already nabbed three hours before the pool opened at his hotel.

The tourist said it was pitch black outside by most of the poolside beds were already occupied by people who appeared to have fallen asleep on them overnight to hold their place.

He said: "It's a bit silly. I do get why people do it, but it's a vicious circle, so to speak. They're the ones creating the problem that they're aiming to avoid. If people didn't reserve beds they didn't need, then there wouldn't be an issue. I haven't seen the beds anywhere near full in terms of people, just towels."

Article continues below

Another holidaymaker, last year, said she and her fiancé were forced to wait for over an hour to get a bed while at a £1,000-a-week hotel.

Laura Smith and her fiancé Eric Whittaker said their holiday was "chaotic" due to the so-called "sunbed wars". She said the hotel implemented a one-hour bed reserve policy to help the situation. This involved pool workers placing a ticket on an unoccupied sun lounger and coming back an hour later to remove the towel if it was still unused.

News.title: Russian warship shadowed for whole MONTH prowling off UK shores
News.content:
Russian warship shadowed for whole MONTH prowling off UK shores

One of Russia's warships is followed around the UK coast in tense operation launched by Royal Navy teams for an entire month amid escalating tension and threats between Kremlin and Britain

View 6 Images HMS Mersey monitors Kremlin ship RFN Admiral Grigorovich (Image: MoD Crown Copyright/PA Wire)

One of Russia’s leading warships has been shadowed for weeks by a string of Royal Navy vessels amid growing tension between the UK and the Kremlin.

‌



For an entire month the frigate Admiral Grigorovich has been watched by patrol ships HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey and HMS Severn as it sailed off the UK coast.

‌



The tense operation lasted for the whole of April and took place west of the UK and in the North Sea including close to the Galloper wind farm, off the Suffolk coast. Sources have said it was one of the most intense shadowing operations undertaken by the Royal Navy in the past decade as Russia has upped its threat level to the UK.

‌



View 6 Images Kremlin threat: President Vladimir Putin (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

OPINION Chris Hughes No way even Trump can try to claim a victory in Iran catastrophe

Iran issues chilling warning amid fears over fragile ceasefire READ MORE :

A Royal Navy spokesman said: “Patrol ships HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey and HMS Severn, tanker RFA Tideforce and Wildcat helicopters from 815 Naval Air Squadron tracked the Russian Navy’s Admiral Grigorovich throughout April. There was not one day last month when the Russian warship, her supporting vessels or the ships she was tasked with escorting was not closely watched by Royal Navy air or sea power.

‌



“The Grigorovich moved between the North Sea and Western Approaches, escorting Russian-flagged vessels heading to and from the Atlantic, Mediterranean and Baltic. She accompanied one submarine and around six merchant and support vessels during the month.

View 6 Images View from Wildcat helicopter: Admiral Grigorovich (Image: MoD Crown Copyright/PA Wire)

“The frigate also paused to take on fuel and supplies near key national infrastructure, including the Galloper wind farm off the Suffolk coast.” The operation emerged as increasingly Russia used its air force and navy vessels to test NATO reaction times and methods to its incursions close to European countries.

‌



Last month UK and Norwegian forces intercepted a month-long covert operation by three Russian submarines. The included Akula-class and GUGI - or Main Directorate for Deep-Sea Research- vessels.

View 6 Images Putin visits crew of Admiral Grigorovich off St Petersbugh (Image: AP)

They were caught surveying critical underwater data and energy cables north of the UK. The mission is believed to have been aimed at hostile reconnaissance or potential sabotage and was monitored but caused no damage.

‌



At the time UK Defence Secretary John Healey delivered a stern warning to Russian President Vladimir Putin. It said: “We see your activity over our cables and our pipelines, and you should know that any attempt to damage them will not be tolerated and will have serious consequences."

View 6 Images Admiral Grigorovich warship anchored in Sudan (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In recent years Russian spy planes have many times made incursions towards UK air space and were shooed off by British warplanes. The operations have been undertaken by UK Typhoons being scrambled to head-off the Russian planes suspected of spying on the UK.

Article continues below

View 6 Images Stern words: UK Defence Secretary John Healey (Image: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Shutterstock)

Talking about the latest operation Fleet Commander Vice Admiral Steve Moorhouse said the crews “demonstrated professionalism, resilience and operational readiness.” He added: “Royal Navy units deployed swiftly to ensure the continuous and seamless monitoring of Russian warships, with multiple assets operating in close coordination to maintain an unbroken posture.

“This sustained effort reflects the Royal Navy’s ability to generate combat-credible forces at readiness, delivering persistent maritime security through leadership, teamwork and operational excellence."

News.title: Simon Calder gives surprising verdict on summer travel chaos fears as 13,000 flights axed
News.content:
Simon Calder gives surprising verdict on summer travel chaos fears as 13,000 flights axed

Simon Calder, the travel journalist and broadcaster, has spoken out following the alarming news of the removal of some 13,000 flights from the May schedule worldwide

View 2 Images Travel expert Simon Calder spoke out about the developments (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/REX/Shutterstock)

Simon Calder has reassured Brits he feels travel chaos this summer is unlikely — despite the removal of 13,000 flights worldwide this month alone.

‌



The travel journalist, 70, was asked about the challenges the industry faces amid the Middle East crisis, which is rocketing jet fuel costs and has led to the cancellations of flights. KLM and Lufthansa made the decision as early as last month to axe some flights across Europe.

‌



But Mr Calder has stressed families shouldn't be concerned their holiday plans will crumble this year. He said: "Keep calm and carry on booking... I’ve talked in the last 24 hours to top people in the travel industry and they’re really frustrated that there’s all this talk of cancellations, when the reality is that people will get their holiday as they expect."

‌



Yet, more than 100 flights from London Heathrow have been cut from the May schedule alone amid fears that the long-term supply of jet fuel could cause further cancellations this summer. Although the government has told us jet fuel levels are sufficient for now, prices of the energy are increasing due to the conflict in the Middle East.

All you need to know about jet fuel crisis as airlines axe flights and holidays at risk READ MORE :

View 2 Images The tail fins of planes are pictured at Heathrow Airport (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Speaking on TV today, Mr Calder continued: "These are actually figures for the month of May, which is low season — they are across the whole world and are included a couple of airlines who have taken out masses of flights, in particular Lufthansa of Germany and Turkish Airlines."

But the journalist said he recognises why families will be alarmed. Holidays for June, July and August will have been booked in considerable advance and these designs may now be in jeopardy.

Dad-of-two Mr Calder added: "Yeah, some people fly on Turkish Airlines, although they haven’t cancelled any routes to and from the UK or any flights. A number of people fly on Lufthansa, and they have cancelled a few Glasgow to Frankfurt, for instance, which is annoying, and passengers are being sent to Edinburgh instead. But it’s 1.5% of the capacity."

Article continues below

Oil prices have soared since the start of the US-Iran war more than two months ago, when the US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian sites. Iran retaliated by striking sites across the Middle East and closing the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, through which 20% of global oil traded passes.

A government spokesperson said: "UK airlines are clear that they are not currently seeing a shortage of jet fuel. Aviation fuel is typically bought in advance and airports and suppliers keep stocks of bunkered fuel to support their resilience.

"We continue to work with fuel suppliers, airports, airlines and international counterparts to keep flights operating. We are also consulting on measures to help airlines plan realistic flight schedules which will avoid last-minute disruption and protect holidays."

News.title: Trump pays tribute after Ted Turner death by taking a shot at CNN: ‘Destroyed his baby’
News.content:

President Donald Trump on Wednesday paid tribute to CNN founder turned philanthropist and environmentalist Ted Turner, who died at the age of 87, but couldn't resist getting in a shot along the way at the groundbreaking news organization he created.

Writing on Truth Social after news of Turner’s death was broken by CNN, Trump called the late billionaire “one of the Greats of All Time” while claiming he had been “personally devastated” in the wake of his decision to sell the cable network to Time Warner because the owners had taken “his ‘baby’ and destroyed it” by making it “woke and everything is is not all about.”

Trump then pivoted to calling the incoming owners of CNN, right-wing billionaire Larry Ellison and his son David Ellison, “wonderful people” and expressing hope that the pair “will be able to bring it back to its former credibility and glory.”

Writing once more of Turner, he again praised him as “one of the Greats of Broadcast History” and said he’d been “a friend of mine.”

“Whenever I needed him, he was there, always willing to fight for a good cause,” he added.

Trump hailed the CNN founder as ‘one of the Greats of All Time’ ( Getty )

Though Trump and Turner both traveled in high-flying media and financial circles in the 1980s, the president’s description of the late icon as something other than “woke” flies in the face of Turner’s own history.

The billionaire mogul, who pioneered cable television in the 1970s and 1980s before devoting his assets to environmentalism and reviving interest in professional sports, was famously liberal and outspoken on numerous political matters.

He once called it a “disgrace” that the U.S. was “the only first-world country that doesn't have universal healthcare” during one 2016 interview, and at a Reuters event in 2006 he suggested it is hypocritical for the U.S. to criticize Iran for wanting to have nuclear weapons.

He said at the time: “They're a sovereign state. We have 28,000. Why can't they have 10? We don't say anything about Israel‍—‌they've got 100 of them approximately‍—‌or India or Pakistan or Russia.”

And while Trump has spent years deriding the concept of climate change as a “hoax,” Turner was long a proponent of drastic actions to reduce what was once referred to as global warming.

In a 2008 interview with PBS, he warned that if steps were not taken to halt rising temperatures, most of the world’s population would die with the survivors left to be “cannibals.”

He also advocated for limiting population growth, stating in the same interview that American families should limit themselves to two children each.

Trump has spent years attacking Turner’s signature creation and the journalists who work there in retaliation for CNN’s aggressive coverage of his political campaigns and his administrations.

Over his decade-long political career, he has called the outlet "fake news," "terrible," and "the enemy of the people,” baselessly accused journalists there of fabricating "phony stories," and called its’ coverage of the war he started with Iran over two months ago as "seditious."

During his first term, his administration unsuccessfully tried to block the purchase of CNN’s then-parent company, Time Warner, by AT&T.

And late last year, he successfully bullied Netflix into dropping a bid to purchase CNN owner Warner Brothers Discovery in order to allow the Ellisons, both of whom are longtime donors and supporters of his, to acquire the company — and the news channel — by merging it with Paramount.

Boisdale restaurant, a short walk from Victoria station in Belgravia, had been a popular hotspot for the centre-right political crowd in Westminster for at least two decades when it became the focal point of opposing Tony Blair’s indoor smoking ban.

But in recent months, Tory MPs who would have ordinarily frequented the venue have been avoiding it, because being seen there was a sure sign that they were planning to defect to Reform UK.

The restaurant has become an unofficial centre of operations for Nigel Farage and his party, where interviews and negotiations over defections took place accompanied by oysters, venison, and claret.

open image in gallery Party leader Nigel Farage with defector Robert Jenrick at Heathrow airport in March ( Getty )

But from Friday, Conservative MPs and peers may feel that it is safe to return with the passing of the 7 May deadline set by Mr Farage for defectors to be accepted in Reform.

And despite suggestions that there could be a stampede to Reform by Tory MPs, the defections have in fact long since dried up, with the last MP to switch sides being former home secretary Suella Braverman on 26 January.

Since then only the arrival of ex-Newham mayor Sir Robin Wales from Labour on 4 March has been a defection of any significance.

In the meantime, the lure of Rupert Lowe’s Restore Britain on the right has seen a steady stream of defections from Reform members, including seven councillors.

Nigel Farage set the deadline of 7 May – the same day as the local and devolved elections – on 15 January at the press conference where he welcomed Mr Jenrick to Reform.

It was a message to Tory MPs, in particular. Mr Farage said that the elections on 7 May would be the day the Conservative Party stopped being a national party, such would be its losses.

The idea was that Tories on the right who had been nervously weighing up whether they defected to Reform would stop dithering and just do it.

But since then only Romford MP Andrew Rosindell on 18 January followed by Ms Braverman eight days later took the plunge.

From a watch list of 11 Tory MPs revealed in The Independent following Jenrick’s defection, only Rosindell and Braverman actually switched allegiances.

open image in gallery Despite an expected flurry of Tory defectors to Reform, Suella Braverman – on January 26 – was the last Conservative MP to switch sides ( PA )

Reform targets like Katie Lam, Lewis Cocking, Sir John Hayes, Mark Francois, Esther McVey, Sir Desmond Swayne, Matt Vickers, Joy Morrisey and Bradley Thomas stayed put.

Even Tory peers like Lord David Frost and Lord Stewart Jackson, who had been rumoured to be ready to move and had less to lose potentially than MPs, did not join Reform. If all those who had been expected to defect had done so then it may well have been curtains for the Conservatives after 300 or so years of history, with a critical mass switching to Reform.

But instead the deadline did not provide the incentive Mr Farage may have hoped for.

Tory Party 2.0

Whether the parliamentarians who defected to Reform did so because they believed in what Mr Farage was selling has been widely disputed.

Mr Jenrick switched out of ambition. The former minister was sacked from Ms Badenoch’s shadow cabinet after it emerged that he had been plotting to defect when screenshots of Jenrick’s defection letter and media strategy were handed to the Tory leader’s office, exposing a plan to attempt to strike a devastating blow to his former party as he jumped ship.

He had calculated that he could not replace Kemi Badenoch as Tory leader and would stand a much better chance of being a potential heir to Farage at Reform.

Meanwhile, according to friends of fellow defector Mr Rosindell, his decision to swap parties was much more linked to his status as “Mr Romford” than any ideological reasons.

open image in gallery Andrew Rosindell (right) with Nigel Farage in Romford in April ( PA )

“All Andrew’s [Tory] councillors were about to go to Reform so he felt he had to go with them,” said one Conservative MP.

Ms Braverman’s husband had previously been a signed-up member of Reform UK, while she had become so detached from the Tories that she had rarely been seen in parliament.

Reform’s Scottish leader Lord Malcolm Offord was another who was struck with ambition. According to Conservative sources, his demands to be the Tory leader in the Lords had been rebuffed and days later he was standing on a podium next to Mr Farage.

Others including Sir Jake Berry, Nadine Dorries, Marco Longhi, Jonathan Gullis and Dame Andrea Jenkyns were no longer in parliament. Only Danny Kruger appears to have joined for ideological reasons.

But even though Mr Farage failed to get the critical mass of defections he had hoped for, the number of ex-Tories in senior positions had been a concern for the Reform base and original supporters.

According to one support tracker, around 9 per cent of Reform’s support is “wobbly” and does not like the party “being Tory 2.0”.

One long-time ally of Mr Farage said: “People do not want failed Tories back in government. They want something new and Nigel has allowed himself to get distracted.”

This is why Mr Lowe’s new party is picking up so many former Reform members.

But Tory MPs who were targets disagree with the “Tory 2:0” tag.

Privately several have said that the lack of policies, the way Reform “took out” their friends at the last election, the concerns over racists in Reform and the suspicion the party is made up of “grifters on the take” with scandals over Farage receiving £5 million and Richard Tice not paying tax, have all contributed to Reform not being an attractive landing spot.

As one Conservative MP put it: “Why would I want to join a party which is not really conservative, is never in parliament for the big votes on Chagos or veterans, where the leaders only believe in themselves and not in values?”

Since his election as leader of the Greens last year, Zack Polanski has seen his party soar in the polls and its membership swell.

After winning a historic victory in the Gorton and Denton by-election, where their candidate beat Nigel Farage’s Reform to take the seat, they are predicted to be one of the big winners of Thursday’s local elections in England.

But Mr Polanski’s popularity ratings have taken a major hit following a row with the chief of the Metropolitan Police over a post he shared about the Golders Green stabbings, with his ‘net approval’ falling 14 points.

Here we take a look at that misstep and others:

Claiming hypnotherapy could lead to bigger breasts

The Green leader has repeatedly apologised for suggesting hypnotherapy could increase breast size.

He has faced criticism since he made the controversial remark to a journalist from The Sun in 2013, before entering politics.

Asked about the article last year, when he announced his bid to stand for his party’s leadership, he expressed regret, saying he was at the time “a young Londoner who was holding down four jobs”.

“I think I saw it as a way to talk about body image and work that can happen where people don’t go under surgery, but can actually feel better about themselves,” he said. “What I’m careful about, though, is that that is not justification … I’ve apologised for it, and I stick by that apology.”

He has also said that he was misrepresented and apologised the following day, recognising it would be offensive.

However, a recently resurfaced BBC Radio Humberside interview from 18 June 2013, six days after the initial report, appears to show Mr Polanski doubling down on his theory.

“Actually increasingly more and more as I work with people, there’s starting to become anecdotal evidence, at least, of a growth in breast size,” he told presenter Peter Levy.

open image in gallery Zack Polanski has said the antisemitic comments made by candidates are 'unacceptable' ( PA )

False claim he was British Red Cross spokesperson

Mr Polanski has acknowledged he was wrong to say he was a spokesperson for the British Red Cross.

He made the claim as he campaigned to become his party’s deputy leader back in 2022.

Asked about the reports, he admitted he “used the wrong word” and said the offending post had been removed.

He explained that he had “hosted various fundraisers for the British Red Cross, and indeed I would go on stage and speak for them about the amazing work they do tackling humanitarian crises, on the climate crisis, and indeed, for refugees all around the world”.

He added: “I used the wrong word, and I accept that, but I would essentially take words on stage with me and speak.

“It’s important, though, and I accept this, that they don’t support any political party, and I’ve made sure that’s been taken down.”

Apology for sharing criticism of the police

Mr Polanski apologised after he came under fire from the head of the Metropolitan Police for sharing an “inaccurate” post on social media criticising the response to the Golders Green terror attack.

Mr Polanski retweeted an X post accusing Met officers detaining the suspect of “repeatedly and violently kicking a mentally ill man in the head” when he was already incapacitated from being tasered.

In a statement, he later said that “everyone in leadership has a responsibility for lowering the temperature at a time of such tension, and I apologise for sharing a tweet in haste.

“Police responses to emergency situations such as these do need later reflection in the right forums, but I accept that social media is not the appropriate channel for doing so.”

But Keir Starmer said his “disgraceful” actions showed he was “not fit to lead any political party”.

open image in gallery Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley (Dan Kitwood/PA) ( PA Wire )

Wrongly said terror suspect was handcuffed in video that sparked incendiary row with the Met boss

The Green Party also says Mr Polanski misspoke when he incorrectly claimed the Golders Green terror suspect was handcuffed in the video that set off the row.

In an interview on the BBC’s Today programme, Mr Polanski said he was “traumatised by seeing someone handcuffed and repeatedly kicked in the head."

But the video, widely circulated online, clearly shows the man is not in handcuffs and officers are grappling to get something out of his hands. The police officers also appear to shout “'drop the knife” a number of times.

Linda Perry, the acclaimed singer and guitarist from 4 Non Blondes, is set to receive a prestigious special international award at the 2026 Ivor Novello Awards.

The 61-year-old US musician will be honoured for her profound influence on the UK music industry, an announcement coinciding with an Amazon Music mini-documentary, Anatomy Of An Earworm, which delves into the creation of her hit song “Beautiful”, famously recorded by Christina Aguilera.

Expressing her gratitude, Perry stated: "It’s an honour to be recognised for my song-writing contributions at the 71st Ivor Novello Awards. So many incredible artists have been celebrated and I am humbled to be standing alongside them."

The Massachusetts-born star first rose to prominence as the driving force behind alternative rock band 4 Non Blondes, penning their UK top 10 smash “What’s Up?”, alongside tracks like “Spaceman”, “Dear Mr President” and “Pleasantly Blue”.

open image in gallery 4 Non Blondes singer and guitarist Linda Perry, who is to receive a special international award at the 2026 Ivor Novello Awards ( PA )

Beyond her band, Perry has forged a remarkable career as a songwriter for a constellation of pop icons, including Christina Aguilera, P!nk, Gwen Stefani, Alicia Keys, Celine Dion, Miley Cyrus, Adele, and Ariana Grande. Her notable compositions for other artists include P!nk’s “Get The Party Started” and Gwen Stefani’s “What You Waiting For?”

Tom Gray, chairman of The Ivors Academy, lauded Perry's distinctive style, remarking: "With defiance, vulnerability and honesty, Linda’s song-writing is instantly recognisable. She has continuously captured both hearts and the airwaves. You just know her songs will endure and continue to resonate."

Roberto Neri, chief executive of The Ivors Academy, added: "Linda Perry’s song-writing continues to have a profound impact on global popular culture. We are proud to honour her with the special international award at The Ivors, celebrating her incredible music and authentic craft."

open image in gallery ( PA )

In other news, Perry recently announced her first solo album in 25 years, Let It Die Here, slated for release on 8 May. Her upcoming accolade follows Spanish singer-songwriter Rosalia being named international songwriter of the year at the prestigious awards ceremony. The 71st Ivor Novello Awards will take place at Grosvenor House in London on 21 May, where the winners across the event’s main categories will be unveiled.
